title: Level 3 Electrical Installation
subtitle: Five copied ElectricianTraining Level 3 mock tests
description: A source-matched Level 3 Electrical Installation exam set copied from the ElectricianTraining mock tests. It adds higher-level electrical science, design, inspection, fault diagnosis, three-phase, machinery and installation-practice questions.
format: Five rotating 30-question source mocks. Pass at 60%+ to match the source.

sections.title: ElectricianTraining Level 3 Electrical Installation Mock Exams

questions.prompt: What can 200 M Ω also be expressed as?
questions.explanation: The prefix mega means one million, or 10^6. Therefore 200 MΩ is 200 x 10^6 Ω.

questions.prompt: In the triangle shown, what is the length of side 'a'?
questions.explanation: Using the dimensions shown on the triangle and applying the appropriate triangle calculation gives side a as 6 cm. The answer is a length, so the centimetre option is the valid result.

questions.prompt: What is the volume of a room that measures 3 m in width, 8 m in length, and the ceiling is 2.4 m high?
questions.explanation: Volume is length x width x height. 3 m x 8 m x 2.4 m = 57.6 m³.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of measurement for temperature?
questions.explanation: Kelvin is the SI base unit for thermodynamic temperature. Celsius is commonly used in practice, but it is not the SI base unit.

questions.prompt: Hertz is the SI unit of measurement for what quantity?
questions.explanation: Frequency measures how many complete cycles of an alternating quantity occur each second. The hertz is defined as one cycle per second, making it the SI unit for frequency; UK mains, for example, runs at 50 Hz.

questions.prompt: What is the formula used to determine Impedance?
questions.explanation: Impedance in an AC circuit is the vector combination of resistance and reactance. The selected formula uses the square-root relationship for that impedance triangle.

questions.prompt: How must a voltmeter be connected to measure the potential difference across a load in a DC circuit?
questions.explanation: A voltmeter must be placed in parallel so it measures the potential difference across the load. Its high resistance prevents it from significantly changing the circuit current.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following formulae is used to determine weight?
questions.explanation: Weight is the force caused by gravity acting on a mass. The correct formula is weight = mass x gravitational field strength.

questions.prompt: Which device is a claw hammer being used as when extracting a nail from a piece of wood?
questions.explanation: A claw hammer pulling a nail pivots about its head and multiplies effort at the handle. That is the action of a lever.

questions.prompt: Approximately what force is needed to raise the 500 kg mass shown in the diagram?
questions.explanation: A 500 kg mass has a weight of about 5000 N. The pulley arrangement shown gives a mechanical advantage, so the required effort is approximately 1250 N.

questions.prompt: What is stored energy also known as?
questions.explanation: Potential energy is stored energy due to position or condition. Kinetic energy is energy of motion, so it is not the stored form asked for here.

questions.prompt: What is the input of an electric motor with an output of 2.1 kW, that has an efficiency of 85%?
questions.explanation: Efficiency = output / input, so input = output / efficiency. 2.1 kW / 0.85 = 2.47 kW.

questions.prompt: What would be the approximate power required to raise a 500 kg mass to a height of 50 m in 90 seconds?
questions.explanation: Power to lift a mass is work done divided by time: mgh / t. 500 x 9.81 x 50 / 90 is about 2.7 kW.

questions.prompt: What is the input of an electric motor with an output of 5 kW that has an efficiency of 80%?
questions.explanation: Input power is output power divided by efficiency. 5 kW / 0.80 = 6.25 kW.

questions.prompt: Which atomic part flows when current flows?
questions.explanation: Electric current in metallic conductors is the movement of electrons. Protons and neutrons remain bound in the atomic nucleus.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is the best conductor?
questions.explanation: Gold is highly conductive and, crucially, does not tarnish or corrode, giving stable low-resistance contact, which is why it is the keyed choice for reliable connections. Copper is actually slightly more conductive but oxidises, while brass and lead are poorer conductors.

questions.prompt: A conductor measuring 50 m in length has a resistance of 0.4 Ω. What would be its resistance if its length is reduced to 25 m?
questions.explanation: For the same material and cross-sectional area, resistance is directly proportional to length. Halving the length from 50 m to 25 m halves the resistance to 0.2 Ω.

questions.prompt: What is the length of a 4 mm² copper conductor having a measured resistance of 0.089 Ω if the resistivity of copper is 0.0178 μΩm?
questions.explanation: Using R = ρL/A rearranged gives L = RA/ρ. 0.089 x 4 / 0.0178 = 20 m.

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between voltage and current across the resistors for the circuit shown?

options.A: Different voltage, different current across each resistor
options.B: Different voltage, same current across each resistor
options.C: Same voltage, different current across each resistor
options.D: Same voltage, same current across each resistor

questions.explanation: In a parallel circuit each branch has the same supply voltage across it. Different resistor values draw different currents according to Ohm's law.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following statements is correct for a series circuit?

options.A: The current varies across the resistors but the voltage is constant
options.B: The resistance and current varies when the voltage is constant
options.C: The voltage and current remains constant when resistance changes
options.D: The voltage varies across the resistors but the current is constant

questions.explanation: In a series circuit there is only one path, so the same current flows through every resistor. The supply voltage is divided as voltage drops across the resistors.

questions.prompt: For the circuit shown, what would be the voltage reading of voltmeter (V1)?
questions.explanation: V1 is connected across the part of the circuit that has the full 60 V potential difference in the diagram. A voltmeter reads the voltage between its two connection points.

questions.prompt: For the circuit shown, what would be the voltage reading of voltmeter (V1)?
questions.explanation: The voltmeter is across the section whose voltage drop is 50 V from the circuit values shown. Voltage in a series section is found from the relevant resistance share or Ohm's law.

questions.prompt: What would be the total supply current (Is) for the circuit shown?
questions.explanation: The total supply current is found from the supply voltage divided by the circuit equivalent resistance. The values in the diagram give 10.0 A.

questions.prompt: How would the current passing through the 20 Ω resistor be determined for the circuit shown?

options.A: Dividing the supply voltage by 20 Ω
options.B: It would be equal to the total supply current
options.C: It would be half the total supply current
options.D: Multiplying the supply voltage by 20 Ω

questions.explanation: The 20 Ω resistor is in the same series path as the supply current in the circuit shown. Components in series carry the same current, so its current equals the total supply current.

questions.prompt: What would be the total circuit resistance if a parallel circuit contained five resistors all having a resistance of 50 Ω?
questions.explanation: For equal resistors in parallel, total resistance is one resistor divided by the number of branches. 50 Ω / 5 = 10 Ω.

questions.prompt: What would a circuit containing several resistors be classified as if the total resistance is found by adding all the resistors together?
questions.explanation: When total resistance is found by adding individual resistances, the circuit is series. Parallel circuits require reciprocal calculations instead.

questions.prompt: What is the power dissipated in the circuit shown?
questions.explanation: Power is calculated from the circuit values using P = VI, I²R or V²/R as appropriate. The values shown produce 1 kW.

questions.prompt: Voltage drop in a circuit is affected by the resistance of what cable part?

options.D: The line, neutral and earthing conductors

questions.explanation: Voltage drop occurs in the conductors carrying the load current to and from the load. In a single-phase circuit that is the line and neutral conductors.

questions.prompt: What would be the effect of placing a copper clad earth electrode into soil, close to a lead water pipe?
questions.explanation: Dissimilar metals in damp soil can form an electrolytic cell. A copper-clad electrode close to lead pipework can therefore cause electrolysis or galvanic corrosion.

questions.prompt: What would be the effect of placing the south poles of two magnets together?

options.A: The strength of the magnets would be doubled
options.B: The strength of the magnets would be halved
options.C: The two magnets would be drawn together
options.D: The two magnets would be pushed away from each other

questions.explanation: Like magnetic poles repel each other. Two south poles placed together will push apart.

questions.prompt: The role of a company's safety representative is to:

options.A: Be responsible for writing risk assessments
options.D: Represent the company at HSE meetings

questions.explanation: A safety representative's role is to represent employees' interests on health and safety matters. They are not normally the person who writes every risk assessment or represents management.

questions.prompt: An electric machine has a power output of 1500 watts. The input current is 4A and the applied voltage is 400V. The efficiency of the machine will be:
questions.explanation: Input power is voltage x current, so 400 V x 4 A = 1600 W. Efficiency is 1500 / 1600 = 93.75%.

questions.prompt: If a contract is not completed on time the client may enforce a:
questions.explanation: A penalty clause allows the client to recover agreed consequences when the contract is completed late. It is used to enforce the time obligation in the contract.

questions.prompt: The device used to change a.c to d.c in a d.c. generator called is the:
questions.explanation: A commutator reverses the armature connections each half-turn so the external output is DC. Without it, the generated voltage in the armature would alternate.

questions.prompt: An abnormal amount of carbon dioxide in an enclosed work space may cause:
questions.explanation: High carbon dioxide levels reduce the oxygen available to breathe and can affect the nervous system. Dizziness and unconsciousness are expected serious symptoms in an enclosed space.

questions.prompt: A water fire extinguisher has a red body and an indicating rectangle which is:
questions.explanation: Water extinguishers use red identification because they are intended for ordinary combustible materials, not live electrical risks. The matching red panel helps identify the extinguisher type quickly in an emergency.

questions.prompt: Advice on safety matters can be obtained from the:

options.D: Royal Society for Prevention of Accidents

questions.explanation: RoSPA is an organisation dedicated to accident prevention and safety guidance. It is therefore an appropriate source of safety advice.

questions.prompt: In a d.c motor armature, the difference between the applied voltage and the armature voltage drop is created because of the:
questions.explanation: As a DC motor rotates, its armature generates a voltage opposing the applied supply. This opposing voltage is back emf and accounts for the difference from the armature voltage drop.

questions.prompt: The resistivity of a material is defined as the resistance when measured across the opposite faces of a cube of that material, of volume:
questions.explanation: Resistivity is the resistance of a standard cube of material in SI terms. That standard cube is 1 m³, measured between opposite faces.

questions.prompt: When equipment is deemed to be satisfactory for the job in hand it is described as:
questions.explanation: Equipment that is satisfactory for the job is described as fit for the purpose intended. The phrase means it is suitable for the task and conditions of use.

questions.prompt: The procedure put in place by an employer to identify hazards in the workplace is called a:
questions.explanation: A risk assessment procedure is the employer's formal method for identifying hazards and evaluating risks. It leads to control measures before or during the work.

questions.prompt: In a capacitor start motor the capacitor is connected:

options.B: In parallel with the run winding
options.C: In series with the run winding
options.D: In series with the start winding

questions.explanation: In a capacitor-start motor, the capacitor is placed in series with the start winding. This creates a phase shift that produces starting torque.

questions.prompt: Safeguarding the rights of individuals with respect to sensitive information is contained in the:

options.B: Health and Safety at Work Act

questions.explanation: The Data Protection Act protects personal and sensitive information held by organisations. It sets duties for lawful handling, storage and disclosure of data.

questions.prompt: A risk assessment should be carried out:

options.A: After an accident in the workplace
options.D: When work activities may put anyone at risk

questions.explanation: A risk assessment is needed whenever work activities may put anyone at risk. That makes it broader than only after an accident or immediately before switching on machinery.

questions.prompt: When planning work schedules, a building site manager must:

options.A: Co-ordinate the activities of workers from all trades

questions.explanation: A building site manager must coordinate the work of different trades so activities do not clash or create unsafe conditions. Programme coordination is central to site management.

questions.prompt: Supplementary protection against electric shock is provided by a:
questions.explanation: An RCD provides additional protection by detecting residual current leaking to earth and disconnecting quickly. Fuses and circuit breakers mainly protect against overcurrent.

questions.prompt: The reactance of a 1µF capacitor connected across a 50Hz supply is:
questions.explanation: Capacitive reactance is Xc = 1 / (2πfC). With 1 µF at 50 Hz, Xc is about 3180 Ω, or 3.18 kΩ.

questions.prompt: Cage rotor induction motors are considered to be:
questions.explanation: The marked answer reflects that cage-rotor induction motors can be used as variable-speed machines when supplied by suitable frequency control. Their speed depends on supply frequency and slip.

questions.prompt: The main function of a fuse is to protect:
questions.explanation: A fuse is primarily there to protect circuit conductors from overheating under overcurrent or fault conditions. It is not the main device for electric shock protection.

questions.prompt: The rotor conductors of a three phase cage rotor induction motor take the form of solid conductors:

options.A: Connected to the supply via conductors
options.B: Connected to the supply via slip rings
options.C: In series with the rotor windings
options.D: Shorted at each end by rings

questions.explanation: A cage rotor is made from solid bars shorted together by end rings. This forms the squirrel-cage circuit in which rotor currents are induced.

questions.prompt: If the plates of a parallel plate capacitor are increased in area, the capacitance will:
questions.explanation: Capacitance is proportional to plate area. Increasing the overlapping area lets the capacitor store more charge for the same voltage.

questions.prompt: A transistor connected in "common emitter mode and biased to cause saturation voltage will act as:
questions.explanation: A saturated common-emitter transistor has a low collector-emitter voltage and conducts heavily. In switching terms, it behaves like a closed switch.

questions.prompt: If a pure inductor of reactance 100O is connected across a single phase 230 V a.c supply, the power dissipated in the circuit will be:
questions.explanation: In an ideal pure inductor, current lags voltage by 90 degrees. The average real power over a cycle is therefore zero watts.

questions.prompt: Earth leakage currents can occur naturally in electrical equipment, for example, cookers, fridges and freezers. This can cause nuisance tripping if the supply is controlled by a:
questions.explanation: Natural earth leakage creates an imbalance between line and neutral currents. An RCD senses that imbalance and may trip even when there is no hard fault.

questions.prompt: Increasing the excitation, to the electromagnet in an a.c. generator will result in:
questions.explanation: Increasing excitation strengthens the generator field. A stronger magnetic field induces a higher output voltage.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following correctly lists three losses inherent in a d.c machine:
questions.explanation: DC machine losses include iron losses in the magnetic core, copper losses in the windings and mechanical friction losses. Those are inherent operating losses.

questions.prompt: The centrifugal switch in a split phase motor is used to:

options.A: Disconnect the main supply to the start winding above full speed
options.B: Disconnect the run winding when approaching full speed
options.C: Disconnect the start winding when approaching full speed
options.D: Disconnect the starter at full speed

questions.explanation: The start winding is only needed while the motor accelerates. The centrifugal switch disconnects it as the motor approaches running speed to prevent overheating.

questions.prompt: An electric heater dissipates a power of 3.0 kW when connected to a 230 V a.c. supply. The resistance of the heater is:
questions.explanation: For a resistive heater, R = V² / P. 230² / 3000 = 17.6 Ω approximately.

questions.prompt: When a semi conductor diode is connected across an a.c. supply having a peak value of 5 V, the peak inverse voltage across the diode is:
questions.explanation: The marked calculation treats the 5 V value as rms and converts it to peak using 5 x √2. That gives about 7.07 V as the reverse voltage to withstand.

questions.prompt: A circuit has a resistance of 20 O and an inductive reactance of 15O when connected to an a.c. supply. The impedance of the circuit is:
questions.explanation: Impedance in an RL circuit is Z = √(R² + XL²). √(20² + 15²) = √625 = 25 Ω.

questions.prompt: What is the most appropriate method to protect against electric shock when carrying out fault diagnosis work?
questions.explanation: The Electricity at Work Regulations require work on electrical systems to be planned and carried out to prevent danger. Following EaWR duties is the legal foundation for safe fault diagnosis.

questions.prompt: Why would a method statement be used by an experienced operative before undertaking work on an installation to diagnose a fault?

options.A: Ensure Health and Safety requirements are considered
options.B: Ensure effective billing of the work procedure or process
options.C: To monitor customer satisfaction for trade reviews
options.D: To reduce the cost implications of the work to be undertaken

questions.explanation: A method statement sets out the safe sequence of work and the controls to be used. Even experienced operatives use it to make sure health and safety requirements are built into the task.

questions.prompt: Which standard must test leads comply with in order to help avoid electric shock when undertaking fault finding and diagnosis work?
questions.explanation: GS38 gives HSE guidance for safe test equipment, probes and leads. Compliant leads reduce the chance of shock or short circuit during live fault finding.

questions.prompt: Which document should be completed when replacing an existing faulty fan isolator switch?

options.B: A Minor Electrical Installation Works Certificate

questions.explanation: Replacing a faulty fan isolator is a small alteration or replacement on an existing circuit. A Minor Electrical Installation Works Certificate records the work and test results.

questions.prompt: Who would an operative need to keep informed of serious faults found on the lighting circuits in a fully functioning commercial unit?
questions.explanation: Serious faults can affect the client's safe use of the building and business operation. The client or their representative must be kept informed so decisions can be made.

questions.prompt: A client has reported that a number of space heaters have stopped working following extensive use during a cold spell. Which of the following items would be the most likely to be checked during testing for fault diagnosis purposes?

options.A: Circuit supply voltage and protective device status

questions.explanation: When several heaters stop after heavy use, first checks should confirm the circuit supply voltage and whether protective devices have operated. That quickly identifies loss of supply or overload tripping.

questions.prompt: What is the most likely outcome following a small leakage between neutral and earth due to water ingress in the connections of a luminaire?

options.A: High earth fault currents causing the main DNO fuse to operate
options.B: High short circuit currents causing circuit fuses to operate
options.C: Phase sequencing becoming reversed causing machinery faults
options.D: Residual current flow to earth causing the operation of an RCD

questions.explanation: Water ingress can create a neutral-to-earth leakage path. The resulting residual current imbalance is likely to operate the RCD.

questions.prompt: What is the most likely reason for the sound of arcing within a contactor, controlling heaters, each time the load is on and running?

options.A: A dead short in the circuit

questions.explanation: Arcing heard only when the contactor is carrying load points to a loose or high-resistance connection. Load current makes the poor joint heat and arc.

questions.prompt: Where is a short circuit in a cable most likely to be located?

options.A: An over tightened termination in an accessory
options.B: At the joint on the top of the circuit breaker
options.D: Where the containment has mechanical damage

questions.explanation: Mechanical damage is a common place for insulation to be crushed or cut. Damaged containment therefore points to the likely location of a cable short circuit.

questions.prompt: What fault would an experienced operative suspect if the final socket-outlet on a radial circuit was not operating but the rest of the outlets on the circuit were?

options.A: Open circuit at the final socket-outlet on the circuit
options.B: Open circuit at the origin of the circuit
options.C: Short circuit at the final socket-outlet on the circuit
options.D: Short circuit at the origin of the circuit

questions.explanation: If all earlier outlets on a radial circuit work and only the final one is dead, the fault is likely at the final point or the cable feeding it. That is an open circuit at the final socket-outlet section.

questions.prompt: What is the most likely reason for 15 A re-wireable fuse, protecting a radial socket outlet circuit that is reported to 'blow every so often'?
questions.explanation: A fuse that blows only occasionally usually points to intermittent overloading rather than a permanent short circuit. A short circuit would normally operate the fuse immediately each time.

questions.prompt: What precautions would an inspector need to consider when undertaking fault diagnosis work to stairway lighting, in an occupied multi-storey building that has back up supplies?

options.A: Ensure that all access equipment is non-metallic and tagged as 'safe'
options.B: Ensure that the emergency lights are functioning correctly
options.C: Ensure the risk assessments are completed and followed
options.D: Ensure the standby generators are connected to the DNO supply

questions.explanation: Stairway lighting in an occupied building with backup supplies involves public safety and possible multiple sources. Completed and followed risk assessments control those hazards before diagnosis starts.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is the most likely test that will cause damage to sensitive equipment when testing to identify faults within an installation?

options.A: A continuity of protective conductors test
options.D: An earth fault loop impedance test

questions.explanation: Insulation resistance testing applies a relatively high DC test voltage. Sensitive electronic equipment can be damaged if it is left connected during that test.

questions.prompt: What is the main risk when an operative undertakes live fault diagnosis work on an old piece of equipment containing electronic components?

options.C: That RCD testing may not be suitable
options.D: That continuity testing may cause damage

questions.explanation: Live fault diagnosis exposes the operative to live parts, especially in older equipment with less guarding or fragile components. Electric shock is therefore the main risk.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to have a logical sequence in respect of the stages of fault diagnosis and correction?

options.A: To avoid inconvenience to other contractors
options.B: To avoid wasting time and effort
options.D: To ensure compliance with the EaWR 1989

questions.explanation: A logical fault-finding sequence narrows the fault step by step. It avoids repeating tests, missing simple causes and wasting time on unlikely checks.

questions.prompt: At what minimum voltage must an operative consider the use of GS 38 test leads?
questions.explanation: GS38 test leads are required where voltages are high enough to present a shock hazard. The threshold used here is above 50 V AC or above 120 V DC.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following instruments is most appropriate when verifying the isolation of a three phase AC supply to a motor?

options.B: A loop / PSC tester compliant to GS 38
options.D: An approved voltage indicator to GS 38

questions.explanation: A GS38 approved voltage indicator is designed specifically for proving dead on AC supplies. It is the appropriate instrument for verifying isolation on a three-phase motor supply.

questions.prompt: What is the correct unit that would be displayed on an RCD tester when confirming compliance with additional protection?
questions.explanation: RCD trip time is a time measurement, so the tester displays it in milliseconds. Compliance is checked against maximum disconnection times.

questions.prompt: What is the most appropriate method of finding the location of an open circuit in the cpc of a radial socket-outlet circuit supplying a number outlets?

options.A: Using a continuity tester at the mid-point of the circuit
options.B: Using a prospective earth fault test at the end of the circuit
options.C: Using an earth fault loop impedance tester at the origin
options.D: Using an insulation resistance tester on the supply to the circuit

questions.explanation: Testing at the midpoint splits the radial circuit into two sections. The result shows which half contains the open cpc, making the fault quicker to locate.

questions.prompt: What type of circuit would have a minimum acceptable insulation resistance value of 0.5 MΩ between live conductors?
questions.explanation: PELV circuits have a lower required insulation resistance value than standard low-voltage circuits. The minimum acceptable value between live conductors is 0.5 MΩ.

questions.prompt: What would be the approximate voltage drop on a 35 m long radial circuit that has a combined live conductor resistance of 0.54 Ω at 20 °C, and a load current of 16 A?
questions.explanation: Voltage drop is current multiplied by conductor resistance, with resistance adjusted for operating temperature. 0.54 Ω at 20 °C rises to about 0.648 Ω, and 16 A x 0.648 Ω is about 10.36 V.

questions.prompt: What is the most significant factor to consider when needing to replace a DOL starter switch on an old lathe in a small workshop?

options.A: Ability to test the old parts

questions.explanation: For an old DOL starter, repair depends heavily on whether compatible replacement parts are still available. Without parts, replacement of the assembly may be the only practical option.

questions.prompt: What is the most significant factor when deciding upon whether to replace or repair a faulty component on a production line in a meat packing factory with a 24 hour, 7 day week shift pattern during the fault finding process?
questions.explanation: On a 24/7 production line, downtime can be more costly than the component itself. Loss of production is therefore the major factor in deciding whether to repair or replace.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is the main consideration when carrying out major fault diagnosis work in the freezer section in a supermarket?

options.B: Suitable high visibility and warm clothing
options.C: Temporary power supplies for the freezers
options.D: The cost of the replacement equipment

questions.explanation: Freezers must stay cold while major fault diagnosis is carried out. Temporary power protects stock and keeps the business safe while the fault is investigated.

questions.prompt: What is the main consideration after fault diagnosis and rectification work has been undertaken in a small 10 year old commercial installation?

options.A: Access to and size of the installation
options.B: All diagnosis is undertaken out of hours
options.D: The designer has signed the original certificate

questions.explanation: After rectification, certification proves the repair was tested and left safe. It also provides the required record for future inspection and accountability.

questions.prompt: What testing must the home owner be encouraged to undertake quarterly, following the rectification of a fault on an RCD protecting a socket-outlet rated at 13 A for outdoor use?
questions.explanation: RCDs need periodic operation of the test button to confirm the mechanism still trips. Quarterly functional testing is the user check normally encouraged.

questions.prompt: What test result would an experienced operative be looking for, when verifying continuity, following the successful replacement of a short main protective bonding conductor to metallic gas pipe within an installation due to damage?
questions.explanation: A sound bonding conductor should have a very low measured resistance, but not an impossible zero reading. A result above 10 mΩ and below 1 Ω indicates practical continuity.

questions.prompt: Which test instrument setting would be used to test an RCD for Additional Protection?
questions.explanation: For additional protection, a 30 mA RCD is tested at 5 x I∆n to confirm rapid operation. This verifies the device trips within the tighter additional-protection time.

questions.prompt: What is the correct symbol to verify on a data plate when checking to see if a new three-phase piece of equipment is compatible for supply voltage before it is installed?
questions.explanation: Voltage on equipment data plates is denoted by U. Checking U confirms the equipment is suitable for the available three-phase supply voltage.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following regulations must be considered when disposing of compact fluorescent lamps?
questions.explanation: The marked option points to the Electricity at Work Regulations duty to prevent danger while handling electrical equipment. Lamp disposal may also require environmental or WEEE controls in practice.

questions.prompt: Who, under the Electricity at Work Regulations, should the inspector ensure the safety of?

options.B: Staff in other buildings owned by the client

questions.explanation: Under the Electricity at Work Regulations, workers must avoid danger to themselves and to other people affected by the work. Inspection and testing must therefore protect both the inspector and others.

questions.prompt: Where is the correct location to test that a lighting circuit is isolated and safe to work on?

options.C: On the load side of the circuit protective device
options.D: On the supply side of the circuit protective device

questions.explanation: Testing on the load side of the protective device proves the downstream lighting circuit has been isolated. That is the part of the installation the person is about to work on.

questions.prompt: How many keys must be available for a lock that is used to securely isolate a protective device?
questions.explanation: A lock-off key should be under the control of the person doing the work. Having only one key prevents someone else from removing the lock and re-energising the circuit.

questions.prompt: Why is safe isolation carried out?

options.A: To allow earth fault loop impedance testing
options.C: To stop RCDs operating when testing
options.D: To stop contact with live parts

questions.explanation: Safe isolation is carried out to make sure workers cannot come into contact with live parts. It removes the electrical danger before work starts.

questions.prompt: Testing is to be carried out at the origin of a large, unoccupied building which has a standby generator. What must be done before tests are carried out?

options.A: Isolate only the normal supply at the origin
options.B: Confirm the standby generator is running before testing
options.C: Check the operation of the standby supply
options.D: The standby supplies must be isolated to ensure safe testing

questions.explanation: A standby generator can backfeed the installation even if the normal supply is off. It must be isolated as well so testing is genuinely safe.

questions.prompt: The implications of not carrying out a safe isolation could lead to prosecution. Which statutory legislation would be used for this purpose?
questions.explanation: Failure to isolate safely can breach the Electricity at Work Regulations. Those statutory regulations are the basis for prosecution for electrical danger at work.

questions.prompt: Which document is statutory?
questions.explanation: The Electricity at Work Regulations are statutory because they are law. Documents such as BS 7671 are important, but they are not themselves Acts or Regulations.

questions.prompt: Which publication does not include model forms that can be used for certification and reporting purposes?
questions.explanation: GS38 is guidance on electrical test equipment and safe test leads. It does not provide model certification or reporting forms.

questions.prompt: Which test would not apply to an electrical installation forming part of a TN-S system?
questions.explanation: A TN-S installation uses the distributor's earth, not a consumer earth electrode as part of the normal earthing arrangement. Earth electrode resistance testing is therefore not applicable.

questions.prompt: Which test could also indicate the supply polarity?
questions.explanation: An external earth fault loop impedance test is made between line and earth at the origin. Because it depends on the correct line-earth relationship, it can also reveal supply polarity issues.

questions.prompt: What is the unit of measurement for recording continuity of protective conductor results?
questions.explanation: Protective conductor continuity is checked as a resistance path back to earth. Because it is a resistance measurement, the result is recorded in ohms, usually as a low value.

questions.prompt: What unit of measurement must an insulation resistance tester indicate?
questions.explanation: Insulation resistance values are normally high, so the tester displays them in megaohms. This makes readings such as 1 MΩ or 200 MΩ practical to record.

questions.prompt: What can be done in order to ensure that instrument readings are accurate?

options.A: Check that serial numbers are present
options.B: Ensure that instruments have BS numbers
options.C: Ensure that the test lead fuses are removed
options.D: Regularly check instruments against known values

questions.explanation: Checking instruments against known values confirms they are reading correctly before relying on test results. It is a practical accuracy check between formal calibrations.

questions.prompt: What does HSE guidance recommend for detachable test leads used on a single instrument?

options.A: They must be at least 2.5 mm² csa
options.C: They must be over 3 m long
options.D: They must only have single insulation

questions.explanation: Different-coloured detachable leads reduce the chance of confusing line, neutral and protective connections. Clear identification is part of safe testing practice.

questions.prompt: What would not be a requirement before using test instruments?

options.C: Ensuring the supply is isolated before commencing dead tests
options.D: Recording details of the instrument supplier

questions.explanation: Before use, the important checks are condition, correct function and safe setup for the test. The supplier's details do not affect whether the instrument is safe and suitable to use.

questions.prompt: What is the most likely reason for continuity of protective bonding conductor results being higher than expected?

options.A: The lead resistance has not been added to the result
options.B: The lead resistance has not been subtracted from the result
options.C: The leads are too long to carry out the test correctly
options.D: The leads are too short to carry out the test correctly

questions.explanation: Test leads have their own resistance, which must be nulled or subtracted for low-resistance continuity tests. If it is left in the result, the reading appears too high.

questions.prompt: What could be the reason for obtaining a satisfactory result, even if the conductor is broken, when testing the continuity of a main protective bonding conductor which is not disconnected at either end?

options.A: The instrument is set on the wrong scale
options.C: The test leads being too long

questions.explanation: If the bonding conductor is still connected at both ends, other metalwork or services may provide parallel return paths. Those paths can hide a break in the conductor being tested.

questions.prompt: Which value would be obtained when a continuity of circuit protective conductors test, is measured at the furthest point on a radial circuit, using a temporary link between line and cpc at the distribution board?
questions.explanation: Linking line to cpc at the distribution board and measuring at the far end includes both conductors in the loop. The measured value is therefore R1 + R2.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not a reason for conducting a ring final circuit continuity test?

options.A: To check that the cable insulation is sufficient
options.B: To check the circuit is in the form of a ring with no interconnections
options.C: To check the continuity of the line, neutral and protective conductors
options.D: To check the correct connection of each item on the circuit

questions.explanation: Ring final continuity tests prove conductor continuity, ring form and correct connections. Cable insulation condition is checked by an insulation resistance test instead.

questions.prompt: What would be indicated by the readings below, during a test of ring final circuit continuity? Line – Line loop reading = 0.1 Ω Neutral – Neutral loop reading = 0.1 Ω cpc – cpc loop reading = 0.167 Ω

options.A: The cpc is a larger csa than the live conductors
options.B: The cpc is a shorter length than the live conductors
options.C: The cpc is a smaller csa than the live conductors
options.D: The cpc is the same csa as the live conductors

questions.explanation: A smaller cpc has a higher resistance than the line and neutral conductors of the same length. The higher cpc-cpc loop reading therefore indicates the cpc has the smaller cross-sectional area.

questions.prompt: What would be the minimum acceptable value of insulation resistance for a 230 V lighting circuit?
questions.explanation: For a 230 V low-voltage lighting circuit, the minimum acceptable insulation resistance is 1 MΩ. Lower readings suggest insulation damage or connected equipment affecting the result.

questions.prompt: What would be the insulation resistance of cable, when the length is doubled, if the original value is 10 MΩ?
questions.explanation: Insulation resistance is inversely related to cable length because more insulation area gives more leakage paths. Doubling the length halves 10 MΩ to 5 MΩ.

questions.prompt: What should be confirmed during a test for polarity?

options.C: Outer metal contacts of ES lamps are connected to the line conductor
options.D: Single-pole switches and devices are connected in the line conductor only

questions.explanation: Polarity testing confirms single-pole switches and protective devices are in the line conductor only. That ensures equipment is not left live internally when switched off.

questions.prompt: Which instrument should be used for testing polarity of the incoming supply to an installation?
questions.explanation: An approved voltage indicator is suitable for checking live polarity at the incoming supply. It is safer and more appropriate for live voltage confirmation than dead-test instruments.

questions.prompt: The BS 7671 maximum tabulated earth fault loop impedance value for a protective device is 2.73 Ω. What is the maximum measured value of earth fault loop impedance permitted for a circuit protected by this device?
questions.explanation: Measured Zs is commonly limited to 80% of the tabulated maximum to allow for conductor temperature rise. 2.73 Ω x 0.8 = 2.184 Ω, rounded to 2.18 Ω.

questions.prompt: What would be recorded as Ipf when PEFC and PSCC at the origin of a three-phase installation are tested using a single-phase instrument, and values of 0.9 kA and 1.5 kA were measured respectively?
questions.explanation: For a three-phase installation tested with a single-phase instrument, the prospective short-circuit current value is doubled. 1.5 kA x 2 gives 3.0 kA for Ipf.

questions.prompt: What reading would be recorded on the electrical installation certificate if the prospective fault current for a single-phase electrical installation is measured between line to earth and line to neutral?

options.A: The higher of the two values
options.B: The line to earth value doubled
options.C: The line to neutral value doubled
options.D: The lower of the two values

questions.explanation: The certificate records the highest prospective fault current because protective devices must be able to break the worst-case current. The lower value would understate the duty.

questions.prompt: A test of prospective fault current at the origin of an installation has been carried out. What should the result be compared with?

options.A: The breaking capacity of the main isolator
options.B: The breaking capacity of the main protective device
options.C: The nominal current rating of the main isolator
options.D: The nominal current rating of the main protective device

questions.explanation: Prospective fault current must be compared with the breaking capacity of the main protective device. The device must be able to interrupt the available fault current safely.

questions.prompt: Where is the correct location to connect test leads, within an installation, in order to test an RCD?

options.A: As close as possible to the RCD on the supply side
options.B: As far away as possible from the RCD on the supply side
options.C: At a suitably safe location on the load side of the RCD
options.D: At a suitably safe location on the supply side of the RCD

questions.explanation: RCD tests are made on the load side so the test current passes through the RCD being verified. The test point must also be safe and suitable for connection.

questions.prompt: What could not be verified by the use of a rotating disc type instrument?

options.B: Direction of rotation at the supply terminals of a three phase motor
options.C: Disconnection of protective devices with the specified times
options.D: Phase sequence at the origin of the supply to an installation

questions.explanation: A rotating disc or phase-sequence instrument can show phase rotation, not protective-device disconnection times. Disconnection time needs the appropriate loop or RCD test equipment.

questions.prompt: Which document details the exact dimensions of particular luminaires?
questions.explanation: Manufacturer's data gives the exact dimensions, mounting details and technical characteristics of a luminaire. Design drawings usually show location rather than every product dimension.

questions.prompt: Which document is non-statutory?

options.A: Electricity Safety Quality and Continuity Regulations
options.C: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act

questions.explanation: The IET Wiring Regulations are non-statutory technical regulations, although they are widely used to demonstrate good practice. The other listed items are statutory legal requirements.

questions.prompt: How would a site supervisor be able to account for all persons on a site, should an evacuation happen due to a fire?

options.A: Ensure all deliveries are signed for
options.B: Ensure all escape routes are securely locked
options.C: Ensure all persons park in designated bays
options.D: Ensure all persons sign in when entering the site

questions.explanation: A sign-in record gives the supervisor a current list of who is on site. During evacuation it can be used for a roll call at the assembly point.

questions.prompt: What would be the best way to identify damage to building decorations before electrical work is undertaken?

options.A: Highlight the details on the invoice
options.B: Note the damage in the site diary
options.C: Take photographs after work is undertaken
options.D: Take photographs before work is undertaken

questions.explanation: Photographs taken before work starts provide evidence of the condition of decorations. They distinguish pre-existing damage from any damage caused during the electrical work.

questions.prompt: What is the most appropriate method of protecting soft furnishings from dust caused by drilling a hole into a ceiling?

options.B: Remove furnishings and store off site
options.C: Spray water over the area while drilling
options.D: Vacuum clean furnishings after the work is done

questions.explanation: A dustsheet physically prevents drilling dust from settling on soft furnishings. It is the simplest suitable protection without removing the furnishings from site.

questions.prompt: In which of the following must un-sheathed single-core insulated cable be installed?
questions.explanation: Unsheathed single-core insulated cables need to be installed in a proper enclosure or containment system. Metallic trunking provides that enclosure and mechanical protection.

questions.prompt: What is the most appropriate cable to connect a 230 V handheld portable appliance, to a fixed wiring system?
questions.explanation: A handheld appliance needs a cable that can move and flex without conductor damage. Flexible cable is designed for that duty.

questions.prompt: What is an advantage of using SWA cable over flat profile cable?
questions.explanation: SWA cable has steel wire armour around the insulated cores. The armour gives much greater mechanical strength than flat profile cable.

questions.prompt: What must be used on long straight runs of PVC conduit systems to avoid buckling and distortion?
questions.explanation: PVC conduit expands and contracts with temperature over long straight runs. Expansion couplers absorb that movement and prevent buckling or distortion.

questions.prompt: What type of trunking fitting is shown in the image?
questions.explanation: A flat 90 degree bend changes trunking direction through a right angle in the same plane. That matches the fitting shown.

questions.prompt: What is classed as a cable containment system, suitable for un-sheathed cables?
questions.explanation: PVC conduit is an enclosed cable containment system suitable for single insulated conductors. Tray, basket and capping do not fully enclose unsheathed singles.

questions.prompt: A conduit is 5 m in length and contains 2 bends. What size conduit is required for the stranded single-core cables shown in the image?
questions.explanation: Conduit size is selected by adding the cable factors and applying the conduit factor for the run length and bends. For the shown stranded singles in a 5 m run with two bends, the required size is 25 mm.

questions.prompt: How many 6 mm² PVC single-core cables can be installed in a 100 x 75 mm trunking?
questions.explanation: Trunking capacity is found from the trunking factor and the cable factor for 6 mm² singles. A 100 x 75 mm trunking has capacity for 150 of those conductors under the stated method.

questions.prompt: Which of the following cables is best suited for temporary supplies in harsh locations, such as construction sites?
questions.explanation: Arctic flex is designed to remain flexible in cold and harsh temporary environments. That makes it suitable for construction-site temporary supplies.

questions.prompt: What procedure should be followed if a power tool required for a task, is found with a damaged flex?

options.A: Carry on regardless as everything is on an RCD
options.B: Carry out the task and report the problem afterwards
options.C: Report the item to a supervisor and do not use the power tool
options.D: Tape over the flex and carry out the task

questions.explanation: A damaged flex can expose live conductors or create overheating and shock risks. The tool should be taken out of use and reported rather than repaired informally or used.

questions.prompt: What is used to ensure an accessory is level?
questions.explanation: A spirit level directly shows whether an accessory is level horizontally or vertically. It is the normal hand tool for setting accessories square.

questions.prompt: What is the most suitable hand tool for cutting lengths of cable tray?
questions.explanation: Cable tray is metal, so a hacksaw is the appropriate hand tool for cutting it to length. Wood saws or keyhole saws are not suitable for that material.

questions.prompt: What type of wall would the device in the image be used for?
questions.explanation: The fixing shown is intended for hollow dry-lined surfaces. Plasterboard fixings grip behind the board where there is no solid masonry to plug into.

questions.prompt: What is the conduit fixing device shown in the image?
questions.explanation: A spacer bar saddle supports conduit while holding it away from the surface. That spacing helps alignment and access around the conduit.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum distance between supports for a horizontal insulating trunking, having a cross-sectional area of 800 mm²
questions.explanation: Small horizontal insulating trunking needs close support to prevent sagging. For an 800 mm² cross-sectional area, the maximum support spacing is 0.5 m.

questions.prompt: What must be installed to protect a 230 V cable that is concealed in a wall to a depth of 20 mm and runs diagonally to an accessory?
questions.explanation: A concealed cable less than 50 mm deep and running diagonally is outside the recognised safe zones. Earthed metal conduit gives mechanical protection and an earth path if the cable is penetrated.

questions.prompt: What is the most suitable method of repairing a ceiling plasterboard having a hole left by a recess downlight which has been removed?

options.A: Apply cement to the wall and rub down to give smooth finish
options.B: Cut a square of white paper and staple over the hole
options.C: Insert a similar sized piece of plasterboard with support behind and finish by skimming with plaster
options.D: Stick small pieces of wet toilet tissue to the sides of the hole and work towards the centre until complete

questions.explanation: A proper plasterboard patch restores the board with support behind it and a skimmed finish. It is mechanically sound and maintains the ceiling surface better than temporary coverings.

questions.prompt: What describes an overcurrent in an otherwise healthy circuit which is caused by mis-use or abuse of the circuit loading?
questions.explanation: An overload is excessive current in a circuit that is otherwise electrically healthy. It is caused by too much load or misuse, not by a short circuit or earth fault.

questions.prompt: What protective device operates by both magnetic and thermal trips?
questions.explanation: BS EN 60898 circuit breakers use thermal operation for overloads and magnetic operation for short circuits. That is why they have both trip mechanisms.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum earth fault loop impedance for a 32 A Type C circuit breaker as given in the IET On-site Guide?
questions.explanation: The On-site Guide tabulated maximum Zs for a 32 A Type C circuit breaker is 0.55 ohms. Staying at or below this value allows the device to disconnect within the required time.

questions.prompt: What is the rated short circuit capacity of a BS 3036 S1A fuse as given in the IET On-site Guide?
questions.explanation: The BS 3036 S1A fuse has a rated short-circuit capacity of 1 kA in the cited table. The protective device must not be used where prospective fault current exceeds its breaking capacity.

questions.prompt: A circuit has been poorly designed for selectivity between an appliance fuse and a circuit breaker protecting the entire final circuit. What is the most likely outcome should a single fault occur on the appliance?

options.A: A fault would cause no loss of any equipment
options.B: A fault would cause the entire supply system to disconnect
options.C: A fault would cause the loss of all equipment on the circuit
options.D: A fault would disconnect the appliance fuse only

questions.explanation: Poor selectivity means the upstream circuit breaker may trip before or along with the appliance fuse. A single appliance fault can therefore disconnect all equipment on the final circuit.

questions.prompt: What should a water heater that is fitted to a 20 litre vessel be connected to?

options.B: A fused spur on a ring-final circuit
options.D: An un-fused spur on a ring-final circuit

questions.explanation: A 20 litre water heater is a substantial fixed load and should not rely on a shared ring-final spur. A dedicated circuit gives appropriate capacity, isolation and protection.

questions.prompt: What condition will the circuit be for a self contained, non-maintained emergency light, in normal situations?

options.A: Only live during a mains failure

questions.explanation: A self-contained non-maintained emergency light is normally energised so its battery charger and monitoring circuit remain supplied. The lamp operates on mains failure, but the unit needs a permanent live feed.

questions.prompt: What provides undervoltage protection on a rotating machine in a factory?

options.A: A circuit breaker protecting the machine circuit
options.B: A contactor connected in the machine supply circuit
options.C: An RCD fitted to the supply circuit
options.D: A surge protective device fitted at the origin

questions.explanation: A contactor coil drops out when the supply voltage falls too low. This provides undervoltage protection and prevents unexpected automatic restarting when voltage returns.
